name: LoopRight Pattern Catalog
description: Engineering-grade loop patterns for designing, reviewing, repairing, and validating bounded, measurable, failure-aware loops.

patterns.title: Retry Loop
patterns.summary: Retry transient failures without duplicating side effects or hiding terminal errors.
patterns.useWhen: Use when an operation can fail temporarily and can be safely attempted again under a bounded policy.
patterns.prompt: Review or implement this retry loop with a transient-failure allowlist, attempt or deadline budget, backoff with jitter when shared systems are involved, idempotency for side effects, and final evidence that records attempts and stop reason.

contract.objective: Complete one operation or fail with a clear terminal reason.
contract.state: Attempt count, delay, last transient error, idempotency key, elapsed time.
contract.progress: Attempt count advances and terminal success or failure becomes known.
contract.invariant: The operation target and idempotency identity remain stable across retries.
contract.budget: Maximum attempts, deadline, cost, or caller cancellation.
contract.stop condition: Operation succeeds or returns a known duplicate-success terminal status.
contract.failure condition: Permanent error, invalid input, exhausted budget, cancellation, or unsafe side-effect risk.
contract.recovery: Back off, jitter, preserve diagnostics, and retry only allowed transient failures.
contract.evidence: Attempt count, elapsed time, final status, and preserved root cause on failure.

redFlags: Bare catch or broad exception retry
Retrying validation, auth, corrupt data, or programming errors
No idempotency key for mutating external calls

verification.title: Retry budget and failure policy are proven.
verification.detail: Tests cover first-try success, transient-then-success, budget exhaustion, and permanent errors that are not retried.

tests: Retries allowlisted transient failure and then succeeds
Stops at max attempts or deadline

patterns.title: Polling Loop
patterns.summary: Wait for external state without hanging forever or missing terminal failure states.
patterns.useWhen: Use when a system must repeatedly read external status until a terminal state is reached.
patterns.prompt: Design or review this polling loop with a deadline or max polls, terminal success and failure states, delay policy, cancellation behavior, and evidence of final status.

contract.objective: Wait until a known resource reaches an explicit terminal status.
contract.state: Current status, poll count, elapsed time, last response, cancellation signal.
contract.progress: Poll count advances and status transitions are observed.
contract.invariant: Only the intended resource is polled and caller cancellation remains respected.
contract.budget: Deadline, max polls, rate limit, or caller cancellation.
contract.stop condition: Status is in the success terminal set.
contract.failure condition: Status is in the failure terminal set, deadline expires, status fetch becomes unsafe, or caller cancels.
contract.recovery: Retry transient status fetch failures with bounded delay and preserve the last useful status.
contract.evidence: Final status, poll count, elapsed time, resource id, and stop reason.

redFlags: Sleep in a loop with no deadline
No handling for failed, cancelled, expired, or unknown states
Fixed aggressive interval against shared services

verification.title: Every terminal state is handled.
verification.detail: Tests cover success, failure terminal state, timeout, transient status fetch error, and cancellation or fake sleeper behavior.

tests: Raises or returns failure on failure terminal state
Stops on deadline or max polls
Uses fake clock or injectable sleeper

patterns.title: Async Fan-Out Loop
patterns.summary: Run many independent async operations without unbounded task creation or unclear partial failures.
patterns.useWhen: Use when processing many I/O-bound items concurrently with async tasks, promises, queues, or worker pools.
patterns.prompt: Review or refactor this async fan-out loop with bounded concurrency, explicit partial-failure behavior, cancellation propagation, cleanup, and tests that prove max active work never exceeds the limit.

contract.objective: Process every input item with bounded concurrency and produce terminal results.
contract.state: Pending input, active tasks, completed results, failed results, cancellation state.
contract.action: Process one item under the concurrency limiter.
contract.progress: Completed plus failed count increases toward total input count.
contract.invariant: Active work never exceeds the configured capacity.
contract.budget: Concurrency limit, queue size, deadline, memory, downstream rate limit, or caller cancellation.
contract.stop condition: Every input item has a terminal result or the caller cancels.
contract.failure condition: Fatal configuration error, cancellation, or failure policy threshold exceeded.
contract.recovery: Record per-item failures, dead-letter where appropriate, and cancel siblings only for fatal errors.
contract.evidence: Result counts, failure records, max observed concurrency, and cancellation test output.

redFlags: asyncio.gather over a huge mapped input
No semaphore, queue, worker pool, or capacity limiter

verification.title: Concurrency and partial failures are controlled.
verification.detail: Tests cover zero input, maximum concurrency, partial failure, fatal failure behavior, cancellation, and result aggregation.

tests: Max active workers never exceeds limit
Individual failures are represented or escalated as designed
Result ordering is documented or tested when required

patterns.title: Distributed Backfill Loop
patterns.summary: Process large historical datasets with checkpoints, reconciliation, and safe resume behavior.
patterns.useWhen: Use for migrations, crawlers, ETL jobs, reprocessing, and large backfills that can span deploys or failures.
patterns.prompt: Design or audit this backfill loop with checkpointing, dedupe, idempotent writes, rate limits, dead-letter handling, resume behavior, reconciliation, and an evidence artifact.

contract.objective: Process every eligible item exactly once or assign it to a terminal exception state.
contract.state: Cursor, checkpoint, processed ids, failed ids, output version, rate-limit state.
contract.action: Read a bounded batch, process items, write outputs, and checkpoint progress.
contract.progress: Checkpoint advances and terminal item count increases.
contract.invariant: No item is written twice for the same output version.
contract.budget: Batch size, runtime window, rate limit, retry budget, cost cap, or daily quota.
contract.stop condition: All eligible items are written, skipped, or dead-lettered.
contract.failure condition: Checkpoint corruption, high error rate, quota exhaustion, schema mismatch, or reconciliation failure.
contract.recovery: Resume from verified checkpoint, skip already-terminal ids, and dead-letter repeated failures.
contract.evidence: Input/output counts, reconciliation report, checksum or sample audit, and dead-letter report.

redFlags: No reconciliation between source and output

verification.title: Backfill completion is reconciled.
verification.detail: Evidence includes source count, output count, skipped count, failed count, checkpoint history, and replay or resume test.

tests: Resumes after interruption without duplicate writes

patterns.title: ML Tuning Loop
patterns.summary: Optimize model or hyperparameter choices without unbounded search or unverifiable improvement claims.
patterns.useWhen: Use for model training, hyperparameter tuning, prompt tuning, ranking optimization, or experiment search.
patterns.prompt: Design or review this tuning loop with objective metric, baseline, validation split, budget, pruning or early stopping, failed-trial handling, reproducibility controls, and a final comparison artifact.

contract.objective: Improve a named metric subject to explicit constraints.
contract.state: Trial number, parameters, metrics, best score, failed trials, random seed, data version.
contract.action: Train, evaluate, and record one candidate.
contract.progress: Trial budget decreases and best valid metric may improve.
contract.invariant: Metric, validation split, data version, and acceptance constraints remain stable.
contract.budget: Trial count, wall-clock deadline, compute budget, max epochs, or early-stopping rule.
contract.stop condition: Budget exhausted, target reached, or no-progress stop triggers.
contract.failure condition: Non-finite metric, invalid config, repeated infrastructure failure, or acceptance constraint violation.
contract.recovery: Mark failed trials, prune unpromising runs, and preserve comparable metrics.
contract.evidence: Baseline, best result, constraints, trial table, best params, seed, and validation split id.

redFlags: No validation split or data version
Accepting against the same signal used to optimize when overfitting is possible

verification.title: Improvement is measured against a stable baseline.
verification.detail: Final evidence compares baseline and selected candidate on the same acceptance criteria and records all budgets used.

patterns.title: Agent Repair Loop
patterns.summary: Let a coding agent inspect, edit, and test without repeating the same failed action forever.
patterns.useWhen: Use when an agent is fixing tests, repairing CI, improving code, or iterating over implementation attempts.
patterns.prompt: Define this agent repair loop with a cycle budget, current hypothesis, one focused edit per pass, deterministic check, repeated-failure detection, preservation of unrelated work, and completion evidence.

contract.objective: Make the named check pass without changing unrelated behavior.
contract.state: Hypothesis, inspected files, edited files, command output, repeated-failure count, remaining budget.
contract.action: Inspect, make one focused edit, and run the relevant deterministic check.
contract.progress: Failure changes, failing count decreases, or a hypothesis is falsified.
contract.invariant: Preserve unrelated user changes and keep edits scoped to implicated behavior.
contract.budget: Edit-test cycles, wall-clock time, commands, tokens, or user-defined cost.
contract.stop condition: Target check and adjacent checks pass.
contract.failure condition: Same failure repeats without changed hypothesis, budget is exhausted, or requirement is ambiguous.
contract.recovery: Change hypothesis, narrow the check, inspect fresh state, or ask for user input when blocked.
contract.evidence: Passing command output, changed file list, cycles used, and concise fix explanation.

verification.title: Agent completion is proven by deterministic checks.
verification.detail: The final answer names the exact passing command, changed files, cycle count, and any residual risk.

patterns.title: Benchmark Loop
patterns.summary: Run experiments until evidence is useful or budget is exhausted, not until optimism wins.
patterns.useWhen: Use for agent evals, prompt comparisons, regression benchmarks, performance tuning, and research sweeps.
patterns.prompt: Design or review this benchmark loop with fixed dataset and versions, objective metrics, sampling plan, budget, failure handling, separation between tuning signal and acceptance evidence, and reproducible artifacts.

contract.objective: Measure or improve a named metric over a fixed evaluation scope.
contract.state: Candidate, dataset version, run id, metric results, cost, failures, random seed.
contract.action: Run one candidate or experiment under recorded conditions.
contract.progress: Results table grows and uncertainty or candidate set shrinks.
contract.invariant: Evaluation scope, metric definition, and recording format remain stable.
contract.budget: Max runs, max spend, max wall-clock time, or statistical stopping rule.
contract.stop condition: Target confidence reached, regression identified, candidate selected, or budget exhausted.
contract.failure condition: Flaky infrastructure threshold exceeded, dataset invalid, or metric becomes non-comparable.
contract.recovery: Mark failed runs, rerun only under documented flake policy, and preserve raw outputs.
contract.evidence: CSV or JSON results, summary table, reproduction command, budget used, and final decision.

redFlags: Try more prompts without a budget
Optimizing and accepting on the same small sample

verification.title: Benchmark result is reproducible and budgeted.
verification.detail: Artifacts include fixed input versions, raw results, summary, reproduction command, and final decision rule.

patterns.title: Durable Workflow Loop
patterns.summary: Review long-running workflows for replay safety, idempotency, compensation, and terminal evidence.
patterns.useWhen: Use for workflow engines, order fulfillment, approvals, sagas, scheduled jobs, and crash-resumable processes.
patterns.prompt: Audit this durable workflow loop for idempotent steps, retry and compensation boundaries, replay safety, timeout behavior, human approval states, and terminal evidence.

contract.objective: Move a business process from start to a terminal state without repeating unsafe side effects.
contract.state: Workflow id, step state, external side-effect ids, retry state, compensation state, approval state.
contract.action: Advance one workflow step or compensation step.
contract.progress: Workflow step state advances toward a terminal outcome.
contract.invariant: Replay never repeats non-idempotent side effects.
contract.budget: Step timeouts, retry limits, approval deadlines, compensation budgets, or workflow lifetime.
contract.stop condition: Workflow is fulfilled, cancelled, refunded, failed, or sent to manual review.
contract.failure condition: Unsafe replay, compensation failure, external terminal failure, approval timeout, or inconsistent state.
contract.recovery: Use durable runtime state, idempotency keys, compensation steps, and manual-review handoff.
contract.evidence: Terminal state, step history, external ids, compensation records, and audit log.

redFlags: Non-idempotent payment or message send inside replayable code
No terminal failed or manual-review state

verification.title: Replay and terminal states are safe.
verification.detail: Tests or review evidence show idempotency keys, compensation boundaries, timeouts, and terminal audit records.

tests: Replay does not duplicate side effects

patterns.title: Autonomous Decision Loop
patterns.summary: Let an agent observe state, propose actions, verify decisions, execute through tools, and update memory without losing permission, audit, or kill-switch control.
patterns.useWhen: Use when an agent loop wakes on a trigger or cadence, reads durable state, proposes a consequential action, verifies it with independent checks, executes through connectors or tools, records outcomes, and updates memory for future runs.
patterns.prompt: Design or audit this autonomous decision loop with an automation trigger, durable state store, maker-checker verification, explicit side-effect permissions, connector idempotency, kill switch, audit log, memory-update governance, and evidence for every executed or skipped action.

contract.objective: Safely convert observed state into verified actions or explicit no-action decisions while preserving auditability and bounded risk.
contract.state: Trigger source, state snapshot, proposed action, verifier verdict, permission status, connector result, risk monitor state, audit record, and pending memory updates.
contract.action: Wake on trigger, read state, propose action, verify with independent checks, execute only permitted side effects, record outcome, and queue reviewed memory updates.
contract.progress: Verified action or no-action records accumulate and unresolved decisions, stale state, or unreviewed memory updates decrease.
contract.invariant: No consequential side effect runs before verification and permission checks, every connector call is idempotent or compensated, and memory updates do not become rules without review.
contract.budget: Cadence, max runtime, max decisions per run, tool-call or cost cap, connector rate limits, approval limits, and risk thresholds.
contract.stop condition: No eligible action remains, a verified action is recorded, human approval is required, the kill switch trips, or a runtime/cost/risk budget is exhausted.
contract.failure condition: Verifier rejects the proposal, deterministic checks fail, state is stale or corrupt, connector idempotency is missing, risk limits are breached, or the audit log cannot be written.
contract.recovery: Abort side effects, freeze or roll back pending actions where possible, mark the decision dead-lettered, escalate for review, and quarantine unapproved memory changes.
contract.evidence: Trigger id, state snapshot hash, verifier verdict, deterministic metrics, permission decision, connector side-effect ids or dry-run output, audit log, risk monitor status, and reviewed memory changes.

redFlags: The same agent proposes and approves consequential actions
State lives only in chat history or prompt memory
Tool calls can mutate real systems without dry run, approval, or idempotency
Lessons are written directly into future rules without review
No kill switch or risk monitor loop
Completion depends on the agent saying the action is safe

verification.title: Every autonomous action is verified, permissioned, and auditable.
verification.detail: Evidence shows the trigger, state snapshot, maker proposal, independent verifier decision, deterministic metrics, side-effect ids or dry-run output, risk guard status, and reviewed memory updates.

tests: Rejects an action when the independent verifier fails
Blocks side effects when permission or idempotency is missing
Stops when the kill switch or risk threshold trips
Records an audit artifact for action and no-action decisions
Queues lessons for review instead of immediately changing future rules
failureModes: Overfitting rules to one bad outcome
